nature-volcano.name: Diamond Head State Monument (Leahi summit trail)
nature-volcano.blurb: The crater-rim climb over Waikiki. Go at 6 a.m.
nature-volcano.check: Nonresidents reserve up to 30 days ahead. Closed Christmas and New Year's Day.
nature-volcano.hours: 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. Last entry 4:30. Closed Dec 25 and Jan 1
nature-volcano.difficulty: Moderate. Steep with stairs, 560 ft gain
nature-volcano.distance: 0.8 mi each way from trailhead. Allow 1.5 to 2 hr
nature-volcano.reservation: Entry and parking at gostateparks.hawaii.gov, up to 30 days ahead. $5 a person, $10 parking

nature-volcano.name: Haleakala summit sunrise
nature-volcano.blurb: Sunrise above the clouds at 10,023 feet, then down Sliding Sands into the crater.
nature-volcano.check: A vehicle reservation is required for 3 to 7 a.m. It opens 60 days ahead at 7 a.m. Hawaii time. Bring winter layers.
nature-volcano.hours: Open 24 hours. Reservation for 3 to 7 a.m. entry
nature-volcano.difficulty: Easy walks at 10,023 ft. Very cold before dawn
nature-volcano.reservation: $1 vehicle reservation at recreation.gov, plus the $30 park pass. Released 60 days ahead at 7 a.m. Hawaii time

nature-volcano.name: Kilauea summit (Kilauea Overlook, Steam Vents, Crater Rim Drive West, Uekahuna)
nature-volcano.blurb: Rim viewpoints over Halemaumau, where Kilauea has been fountaining in episodes.
nature-volcano.check: The eruption is paused between episodes. Check the volcano observatory the week you go.
nature-volcano.hours: Open 24 hours. Lots can fill by 10 a.m.

nature-volcano.name: Kilauea Iki Trail
nature-volcano.blurb: Down through rainforest and across a steaming 1959 lava lake.
nature-volcano.check: Part of Byron Ledge Trail closed Oct 7, which may cut the loop.
nature-volcano.difficulty: Moderate. About 400 ft down and back up

nature-volcano.name: Nahuku (Thurston Lava Tube)
nature-volcano.blurb: A walk-through lava tube in fern forest.
nature-volcano.hours: Open 24 hours, lit 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.

nature-volcano.name: Chain of Craters Road
nature-volcano.blurb: The road from rainforest down to the sea cliffs, past fresh flows.
nature-volcano.check: The Holei Sea Arch at the end collapsed in September.
nature-volcano.distance: About 19 mi one way to the coast

nature-volcano.name: Mauna Ulu lava field and Puu Huluhulu cinder cone
nature-volcano.short: Mauna Ulu lava field and Puu Huluhulu cinder cone
nature-volcano.blurb: The quieter lava-field hike, up a cinder cone over the 1969-74 flows.
nature-volcano.distance: About 2.5 mi round trip to Puu Huluhulu summit

nature-jungle.name: Manoa Falls Trail
nature-jungle.blurb: The closest real rainforest to Waikiki. Muddy, rooty and busy.

nature-jungle.name: Kualoa Ranch Jungle Expedition
nature-jungle.blurb: An open-air ride into a rainforest valley and its film sites.
nature-jungle.check: Rough ride. Current schedule not confirmed.

nature-jungle.name: Pipiwai Trail to Waimoku Falls (Kipahulu District)
nature-jungle.blurb: Maui's best jungle hike: a banyan, a bamboo forest and a 400-foot waterfall.
nature-jungle.check: It closes after heavy rain. Get there before 9 a.m.
nature-jungle.difficulty: Moderate. About 650 ft gain, 2.5 to 3 hr
nature-jungle.reservation: No reservation. $30 park pass per car, good for 3 days

nature-jungle.name: Iao Valley State Monument
nature-jungle.blurb: A short loop into a lush valley under the Iao Needle.
nature-jungle.reservation: Entry and parking at gostateparks.hawaii.gov. $5 a person, $10 parking

nature-jungle.name: Akaka Falls State Park
nature-jungle.blurb: A 442-foot waterfall on a short rainforest loop above Hilo.
nature-jungle.check: Part of the loop is closed by fallen trees.
nature-jungle.reservation: $5 a person plus $10 parking, card only. Pay before you arrive (weak cell signal)

nature-jungle.name: Rainbow Falls (Wailuku River State Park)
nature-jungle.blurb: A roadside Hilo waterfall. Morning brings the rainbows.

nature-jungle.name: Hawaii Forest & Trail volcano tours
nature-jungle.blurb: Naturalist-led volcano hikes from Kona, small groups, long days.
nature-jungle.check: Confirm December routes with the operator.
nature-jungle.reservation: Volcano hike, 10 hours, $259. Volcano, chocolate and waterfalls, 11.5 hours, $295

nature-jungle.name: Hanakapiai Beach and Falls (Kalalau Trail, Haena State Park)
nature-jungle.blurb: The Na Pali cliffs on foot, to a beach or on to a jungle waterfall.
nature-jungle.check: Day reservations at gohaena.com open 30 days ahead. Strenuous, muddy, with stream crossings.
nature-jungle.distance: Beach about 4 mi round trip. Falls 8 mi round trip
nature-jungle.reservation: Entry $5 a person and parking $10, or the shuttle, at gohaena.com. Bookable 30 days ahead

nature-jungle.name: Wailua River kayak (Secret Falls)
nature-jungle.check: Secret Falls and the trail beyond the landing are closed.
nature-jungle.reservation: Paddle on your own to the landing, or book a guided tour

nature-lagoons.name: Kaneohe Bay sandbar (Ahu o Laka)
nature-lagoons.blurb: Shallow turquoise water in the middle of the bay, under the Koolau cliffs.
nature-lagoons.check: Tours sell out. Best at low tide.
nature-lagoons.difficulty: Easy by boat. Moderate paddle by kayak
nature-lagoons.distance: Mid-bay. Distance depends on launch point
nature-lagoons.reservation: Tours sell out. Book a few weeks ahead

nature-lagoons.name: Lanikai and Kailua beaches, plus Kaiwa Ridge (Lanikai Pillbox) hike
nature-lagoons.short: Lanikai and Kailua beaches, plus Kaiwa Ridge (Lanikai Pillbox) hike
nature-lagoons.blurb: Calm windward water and the Mokulua islets.
nature-lagoons.difficulty: Beach easy. Kaiwa Ridge short but steep and slippery
nature-lagoons.distance: About kaiwa Ridge about 1.5 to 2 mi round trip

nature-lagoons.name: Kaena Point (Natural Area Reserve)
nature-lagoons.blurb: Oʻahu's remote western tip, with seabirds and monk seals.
nature-lagoons.check: The west trail is closed. Use the north side.
nature-lagoons.distance: About 2.5 mi each way from either trailhead
nature-lagoons.reservation: Hike in from the north side

nature-lagoons.name: Makapuu Lighthouse Trail (Kaiwi State Scenic Shoreline)
nature-lagoons.blurb: A paved coastal climb with winter whales and a view to Molokai.
nature-lagoons.difficulty: Easy to moderate. Paved, exposed, uphill

nature-lagoons.name: Makena State Park (Oneloa / Big Beach)
nature-lagoons.reservation: $5 a person plus $10 parking, at the kiosk or ParkMobile

nature-lagoons.name: Waianapanapa State Park
nature-lagoons.blurb: Black sand, sea caves and a lava-coast trail on the Road to Hana.
nature-lagoons.check: Nonresident entry and parking reservation required.
nature-lagoons.reservation: Entry and parking at gostateparks.hawaii.gov. $5 a person, $10 parking

nature-lagoons.name: Kiholo Bay (Wainanalii lagoon)
nature-lagoons.blurb: A calm lava-framed lagoon with sea turtles.
nature-lagoons.check: Day use only. The pond itself is private.

nature-lagoons.name: Papakolea Green Sand Beach
nature-lagoons.blurb: The green-sand beach at the south tip, a long walk from anywhere.
nature-lagoons.check: About 2.5 miles each way with no shade. Rides offered there run without permits.
nature-lagoons.difficulty: Moderate. Flat but hot, exposed, rutted

nature-lagoons.name: Waipio Valley Lookout
nature-lagoons.blurb: The rim view into Waipio's cliff-walled valley.
nature-lagoons.check: The valley floor is closed to visitors.
nature-lagoons.reservation: The lookout is free. The valley road is closed to visitors

nature-lagoons.name: Hanalei Bay
nature-lagoons.blurb: Kauaʻi's north-shore bay, with waterfalls on the mountains behind it.
nature-lagoons.check: Winter surf can be big. Swim near lifeguards.

nature-lagoons.name: Tunnels (Makua) and Haena Beach Park
nature-lagoons.blurb: Reef snorkeling under the Na Pali mountains.
nature-lagoons.check: Only on calm days, and parking is tight.
nature-lagoons.difficulty: Easy to moderate snorkel, calm days only

nature-lagoons.name: Waimea Canyon Lookout
nature-lagoons.blurb: Kauaʻi's canyon from its one open lookout.
nature-lagoons.check: Kokee Road and the other lookouts are closed.

outlook.why: Most of Hawaii Volcanoes NP reopened Aug. 28 and Sept. 27. Kilauea is in episodic fountaining (Episode 56 forecast Nov. 1 to 7). State parks reopened except Lapakahi and some camping. Expect vog and short-notice summit closures
Haleakala summit and Kipahulu reopened Sept. 27. DLNR says all Maui parks reopened except Polipoli. Book Haleakala sunrise and Waianapanapa early
Diamond Head and most parks open. Kaena Point west trail closed and Makapuu upper lookout closed until Nov. 4. Diamond Head closed Dec. 25 and Jan. 1

Haena day hikes to Hanakapiai and one Waimea Canyon lookout are open, but Kokee Road, Polihale, Secret Falls, Kauaʻi camping and all other Kauaʻi state parks remain closed after Hurricane Lowell. Winter north-shore surf limits beaches

closed.name: Polihale
closed.note: Closed after the September storm, with no reopening date.
